# 0d Telegram notifications: contract

**Read first:** [notifications](../processes/platform/notifications.md), [Telegram](../integrations/telegram.md), [events](../events.md), the [0c contract](./0c.md) and its **As built** notes (the dispatcher, `Enqueue` in a transaction, `Defer`).

**Done when:** a bot token and a detected chat are saved in Settings → Integrations → Telegram; **Send test** arrives; a failing demo job's `job.failed` arrives in Telegram in the admin's language with an **Open in Proxier** button; Settings → Notifications toggles each event type; the dashboard says "Notifications are not configured" when they aren't and lists failed notifications; every edge case below has its test.

## Decisions

| Topic | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Rules storage | `notification_rules` holds a row only where the admin's choice differs from the catalog default (`events.Type.Notify`). Setting a rule back to its default deletes the row. A toggle records `settings.changed{keys: ["notifications.<type>"]}` on subject `settings:notifications`. | Same pattern as settings (0a): a changed default reaches every install that never touched it. |
| Conditional notify | `events.Type` gains `NotifyIf func(payload map[string]any) bool`. When set, a rule that is on notifies only if it returns true. `auth.signed_in` uses `new_ip == true`. | events.md "on when new_ip". Keeps the rule a plain on/off for the admin. |
| Emoji | `events.Type` gains `Emoji string` (from the table in [telegram.md](../integrations/telegram.md#message-shape)); types whose emoji depends on the payload implement `module.NotificationRenderer`. | |
| Texts | Default rendering: title `notify.<type>`, optional body `notify.<type>.body`, placeholders `{subject}` (the name, plain), `{actor}` and the payload's fields. A module's `NotificationRenderer` takes over for its own types when it returns ok. Rendered **when queued**, in the admin's `language`, with names from `SubjectNamer`s at that moment. | notifications.md "texts describe that moment". |
| Notifier | Dispatcher subscriber `platform.notifier`, every type except `notification.*`. In the cursor transaction: rule off or `NotifyIf` false → nothing; channel not configured → nothing; else insert the notification (`UNIQUE (event_id, channel)`, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`) and enqueue its `platform.notify` job. | Exactly once by construction (0c); the unique key still guards a replay. |
| Not configured | No token or no chat → events are recorded, nothing is queued, and the dashboard band shows. Enabling Telegram later doesn't send old events. | notifications.md; a backlog of stale alarms would be noise. |
| Delivery job | Type `platform.notify`: queue `notify` (concurrency 1), `MaxAttempts` 4, `Backoff` 10 s, 1 min, 5 min, one step `send`. A sent notification is skipped (idempotent). 429 → `jobs.Defer(retry_after)`. `OnFailed`: mark the notification `failed` and record `notification.failed{channel, error}` on subject `event:<id>` — never `job.failed`. | A notify failure that notified would loop. |
| Pace | The Telegram channel waits until 1 s after its previous send before sending. With one worker that gives ≤ 1 msg/s in order. | telegram.md. |
| Telegram client | Own small client (`net/http`, JSON), base URL configurable for tests, 10 s timeout. `parse_mode: HTML`, every interpolated value `html.EscapeString`d by the channel, `disable_web_page_preview: true` (`link_preview_options.is_disabled`), one inline URL button. **Errors never contain the token**: request URLs are rebuilt without it before wrapping `net/http` errors. | No library for three methods; the token is in the URL path, and `*url.Error` prints the URL. |
| Settings | Section `telegram`: `telegram.bot_token` (secret), `telegram.bot_username` (string, from `getMe`), `telegram.chat_id` (string: an integer, or `@channel`), `telegram.chat_title` (string, for display). The section has its own page; the generic form isn't used. | |
| Token save | `getMe` first; a refusal shows "Telegram refused this token" and saves nothing. A good token saves the token and username together. | Edge case "invalid token → nothing saved". |
| Detect chat | `getUpdates` (no offset, `timeout=0`, `allowed_updates` message, channel_post, my_chat_member), distinct chats, newest first. None → "No chats yet. Send /start to @<bot> and try again." The admin picks one, or types an ID. Choosing **saves** it. | Updates are not confirmed, so detecting twice works. |
| Send test | A separate button after the chat is saved; synchronous call from the handler (no transaction open), 10 s timeout, result shown inline. The chat stays saved whatever the result. | Edge case "blocked bot → error shown, saved anyway". |
| Header warning | The warning cell (0b `Shell.Warning`) shows "Telegram failing" when the newest finished notification is `failed`, linking to the dashboard area. | ui/README header "notifications health". |
| Dashboard | Band "Notifications are not configured" → Settings → Integrations → Telegram. Area "Failed notifications": failed in the last 7 days, newest first, each with its event sentence and error, and **Retry** (retries the job). | |
| Retention | Notifications kept 90 days (`platform.retention` from 0c), sent or not, with the text as rendered (payloads never hold secrets, so the text has none). | Matches failed jobs. |
| Rule scope | `notification_rules` is per event type only: Telegram is the only channel. A second channel adds a `channel` column to the key in its own migration. | Nothing in the UI has a channel dimension yet. |
| Event link | `notifications.event_id` has no foreign key. | Events can be pruned (data-model.md) and the notification carries its own message; a nulled id would also break `UNIQUE (event_id, channel)`. |

## Tables — `internal/platform/migrations/00004_notifications.sql`

```sql
-- +goose Up

-- The admin's choices that differ from the catalog default.
-- Per event type: one channel (Telegram). A second channel adds a column to the key.
CREATE TABLE notification_rules (
    event_type TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    enabled    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (enabled IN (0, 1)),
    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
) STRICT;

-- One notification per event and channel, rendered when queued.
CREATE TABLE notifications (
    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    event_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,                -- no foreign key: events can be pruned
    channel    TEXT NOT NULL,                   -- "telegram"
    lang       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (lang IN ('en', 'ru')),
    message    TEXT NOT NULL,                   -- JSON notify.Message, plain text (escaped by the channel)
    state      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('queued', 'sent', 'failed')),
    attempts   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,      -- counted tries (429 waits are not)
    last_error TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    job_id     INTEGER,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    sent_at    TEXT,
    UNIQUE (event_id, channel)
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX notifications_state ON notifications (state, created_at);
-- Retention deletes by age whatever the state.
CREATE INDEX notifications_created ON notifications (created_at);

-- +goose Down
DROP TABLE notifications;
DROP TABLE notification_rules;
```

## Go signatures

### `internal/platform/events` (additions)

```go
type Type struct {
	// … 0a fields
	// NotifyIf narrows an enabled rule: nil means always.
	NotifyIf func(payload map[string]any) bool
	// Emoji leads the notification ("🔐").
	Emoji string
}
```

### `internal/platform/notify`

```go
// Message is a notification as rendered when queued. Plain text: the channel escapes it.
type Message struct {
	Emoji  string `json:"emoji"`
	Title  string `json:"title"`  // "nl-2 is ready"
	Body   string `json:"body"`   // one sentence, optional
	URL    string `json:"url"`    // absolute, the subject's page; "" for no button
	Button string `json:"button"` // "Open in Proxier", translated
}

type Channel interface {
	Name() string // "telegram"
	Configured(ctx context.Context) (bool, error)
	// Send delivers m. *RateLimitedError asks to wait; other errors are retried.
	Send(ctx context.Context, m Message) error
}

type RateLimitedError struct{ RetryAfter time.Duration }

type Rule struct {
	Type    events.Type
	Enabled bool
	Default bool
}

type Service struct{ /* … */ }

func New(d *db.DB, ev *events.Catalog, cat *i18n.Catalog, j *jobs.System, a *auth.Service, baseURL *url.URL, log *slog.Logger) *Service
func (s *Service) AddChannel(c Channel) error
func (s *Service) AddRenderer(module string, r Renderer) error
func (s *Service) AddNamer(n SubjectNamer) error

// Startup wiring.
func (s *Service) Subscriber() events.Subscriber // platform.notifier
func (s *Service) JobType() jobs.Type            // platform.notify

// Settings → Notifications.
func (s *Service) Rules(ctx context.Context) ([]Rule, error) // grouped by module by the caller
func (s *Service) SetRule(ctx context.Context, eventType string, enabled bool) error

// Dashboard and header.
func (s *Service) Configured(ctx context.Context) (bool, error)
func (s *Service) Failed(ctx context.Context, since time.Time, limit int) ([]Notification, error)
func (s *Service) LatestFailed(ctx context.Context) (bool, error)

type Notification struct {
	ID, EventID, JobID int64
	Channel, State     string
	Message            Message
	Attempts           int
	LastError          string
	CreatedAt, SentAt  db.Time
}

// Renderer is module.NotificationRenderer.
type Renderer interface {
	RenderNotification(ctx context.Context, e events.Event, loc *i18n.Localizer) (Message, bool, error)
}
```

### `internal/platform/notify/telegram`

```go
type Client struct {
	BaseURL string // "https://api.telegram.org"
	Token   string
	HTTP    *http.Client
}

type User struct{ ID int64; Username, FirstName string }
type Chat struct{ ID int64; Type, Title, Username string } // Title falls back to the person's name
type Update struct{ ID int64; Chat Chat }

// APIError is a Bot API refusal. Description is Telegram's, never the token.
type APIError struct {
	Code        int
	Description string
	RetryAfter  time.Duration // set on 429
}

func (c *Client) GetMe(ctx context.Context) (User, error)
func (c *Client) GetUpdates(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]Update, error)
func (c *Client) SendMessage(ctx context.Context, chatID, html string, button *URLButton) error

type URLButton struct{ Text, URL string }

// Channel reads its token and chat from settings on every send.
type Channel struct {
	Now   func() time.Time
	Sleep func(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) error
	// …
}

func NewChannel(st *settings.Store, httpc *http.Client, baseURL string) *Channel
func (c *Channel) Name() string
func (c *Channel) Configured(ctx context.Context) (bool, error)
func (c *Channel) Send(ctx context.Context, m notify.Message) error
// Format renders the message as Telegram HTML: "<emoji> <b>title</b>\nbody".
func Format(m notify.Message) string

// Fake is a Bot API on httptest for tests: scripted getMe/getUpdates answers,
// recorded sendMessage calls, injectable 429s and outages.
type Fake struct{ /* … */ }

func NewFake(t testing.TB, token string) *Fake
```

## Platform event texts (EN; RU twins in the catalog)

| Event | Emoji | Title | Body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auth.signed_in` (`new_ip`) | 🔐 | Signed in from a new IP {ip} | {browser} |
| `auth.locked` | 🔐 | {failures} failed sign-ins from {ip} | Locked for {minutes} min. |
| `auth.password_changed` | 🔐 | The admin password was changed | Via {via}. |
| `ssh.host_key_changed` (0e) | 🔐 | Host key of {subject} changed | Work with it is stopped until you accept the new key. |
| `ssh.key_generated` (0e, regenerated) | 🔐 | Proxier's SSH key was regenerated | Every server, jump host and router needs the new key. |
| `job.failed` | 🔴 | {subject} failed | {error} |
| `backup.failed` (0e) | 🔴 | Backup failed | {error} |

`{subject}` of `job.failed` is the job's name, e.g. "Job #421 · demo".

## Routes

| Method, path | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /settings/integrations` | Sub-sections; 0d: Telegram |
| `GET /settings/integrations/telegram` | Token (secret field), bot, chat, Detect chat, Send test |
| `POST /settings/integrations/telegram/token` | `getMe`, then save |
| `POST /settings/integrations/telegram/detect` | Fragment: chats found, or the "No chats yet" message |
| `POST /settings/integrations/telegram/chat` | Save `chat_id` (+ title) |
| `POST /settings/integrations/telegram/test` | Fragment: sent, or the error |
| `GET /settings/notifications` | Toggles grouped by module, each with description and default; filter "all events / changed" |
| `POST /settings/notifications/:type` | `enabled=0\|1` (htmx, per switch) |
| `POST /notifications/:id/retry` | Retry the failed delivery's job |

Keys on Notifications: `space` toggle the row, `j k`, `[ ]` sections (RP-Settings).

## Doc changes in the same commit

- `docs/events.md`: `notification.failed`; the platform rows' texts above.
- `docs/processes/platform/notifications.md`: not configured → nothing queued and no backlog; Send test is separate from saving the chat; notification failures never notify.
- `docs/data-model.md`: Notification holds the rendered message as JSON and `lang`; rules only where they differ from the default.

## Checklist

Notification edge cases ([notifications.md](../processes/platform/notifications.md#edge-cases-each-is-a-test)):

- [ ] Invalid bot token → refused, nothing saved — `pages/integrations_test.go` `TestInvalidBotTokenSavesNothing`
- [ ] Detect chat before `/start` → "No chats yet. Send /start to @bot and try again" — `pages/integrations_test.go` `TestDetectChatWithoutUpdates`
- [ ] Send test to a chat that blocked the bot → error shown, chat stays saved — `pages/integrations_test.go` `TestSendTestErrorKeepsChat`
- [ ] A notifying event (test-declared type with a `SubjectNamer`) → one message with **Open in Proxier** to the subject's page — `notify/notifier_test.go` `TestNotifyingEventSendsOneMessageWithButton`
- [ ] The same event delivered twice → one message — `notify/notifier_test.go` `TestDuplicateDeliveryNotifiesOnce`
- [ ] Rule off → no message, the event is still listed — `notify/notifier_test.go` `TestRuleOffSendsNothing`
- [ ] 30 events in one second → 30 messages, ≥ 1 s apart, in order — `notify/deliver_test.go` `TestBurstIsPacedInOrder`
- [ ] `429 retry_after=20` → waits 20 s, then sent; attempt not counted — `notify/deliver_test.go` `TestRateLimitWaitsWithoutCountingAttempt`
- [ ] Telegram down 10 min → failed after the last retry, shown on the dashboard; later messages still try — `notify/deliver_test.go` `TestOutageFailsAfterRetriesAndLaterMessagesTry`
- [ ] Admin language Russian → Russian text, name untranslated — `notify/notifier_test.go` `TestMessageInAdminLanguage`
- [ ] Subject renamed after queueing → the old name — `notify/notifier_test.go` `TestTextIsRenderedWhenQueued`

The contract's own decisions:

- [ ] `auth.signed_in` notifies only with `new_ip` — `notify/notifier_test.go` `TestSignedInNotifiesOnlyFromNewIP`
- [ ] A rule back at its default deletes its row; a toggle records `settings.changed` — `notify/rules_test.go` `TestRuleRowsOnlyForNonDefaults`
- [ ] Not configured → nothing queued; configuring later sends no backlog — `notify/notifier_test.go` `TestUnconfiguredChannelQueuesNothing`
- [ ] Notification failure records `notification.failed`, no `job.failed`, no notification about it — `notify/deliver_test.go` `TestDeliveryFailureNeverNotifies`
- [ ] A module renderer takes over its types — `notify/notifier_test.go` `TestModuleRendererTakesOver`
- [ ] HTML in names is escaped — `notify/telegram/channel_test.go` `TestFormatEscapesHTML`
- [ ] No error or log line contains the token (bad DNS, refused connection, 401, 500) — `notify/telegram/client_test.go` `TestErrorsNeverContainToken`
- [ ] `getUpdates` parsing: private chat, group, channel, `my_chat_member`; distinct, newest first — `notify/telegram/client_test.go` `TestGetUpdatesFindsChats`
- [ ] Every platform event with `Notify` or `NotifyIf` has `notify.<type>` in EN and RU — `internal/platform/messages_test.go` `TestEveryNotifyingEventHasAText`
- [ ] Dashboard band and failed list; header warning — `pages/dashboard_test.go` `TestDashboardShowsNotificationHealth`
- [ ] Failed demo job reaches the fake Telegram end to end — `internal/platform/platform_test.go` `TestFailedDemoJobReachesTelegram`
